blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Sumas Prairie

Sumas Prairie is the low agricultural prairie in southeast Abbotsford, in the City of Abbotsford, between Abbotsford and Chilliwack. Its September 2026 board row records zero attached listings and zero attached sales, no condo or townhome card appeared in its feed, and no named strata complex on the prairie was confirmed on any official or developer source. Plan currency note. Abbotsford's current Official Community Plan is Abbotsforward 2050, adopted December 2025 — the 2016 OCP is NOT current, and any document citing it as the governing plan is a plan out of date.
Streets, schools and getting around Sumas Prairie

items.t: Sumas Prairie is an FVREB board sub-area of the City of Abbotsford — the low agricultural prairie in southeast Abbotsford between Abbotsford and Chilliwack, plus the upland fringe the feed itself surfaces (Majuba Hill / Old Yale Road cards labelled Sumas Prairie). Street-level board boundary: Not verified — FVREB publishes no street-level boundary for the sub-area, and no municipal boundary was substituted for it.

Watershed geography: Sumas Prairie sits in the Sumas River watershed; the Sumas River Watershed Flood Mitigation Planning Initiative's six signatories are the Province of B.C., the Semá:th, Máthxwi and Leq'á:mel First Nations, the City of Abbotsford and the City of Chilliwack.

That is a near-empty row: no sales in either split, and no pace or price conclusion can be drawn from it. SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, so there is no Sumas Prairie median: Not verified at sub-area level.
Both page claims are not verified as stated.

Flood — the defining fact of this sub-area: the City hosts the Province's release on the Sumas River Watershed Flood Mitigation Planning Initiative, signed in April 2023 in response to widespread flooding on Sumas Prairie from heavy rainfall in November 2021; the Province is providing $3.3 million for critical design and assessment work, and has provided approximately $220 million in recovery, preparedness and mitigation funding for Abbotsford and Sumas Prairie since 2021, including $76.6 million for upgrades to the Barrowtown Pump Station. The same release records that December flooding in the Sumas region again demonstrated the corridor is highly prone to water surges, and that the initiative's studies are at various stages of completion — flood mitigation for the prairie is active planning, not a settled fix.
Health care is outside the sub-area: Abbotsford Regional Hospital and Cancer Centre, 32900 Marshall Rd, and the Abbotsford Urgent and Primary Care Centre, 2692 Clearbrook Rd #100.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Sumas Prairie

items.t: The ALC housing frame on ALR parcels: land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel unless the owner qualifies for an additional residence; the principal residence must have a total floor area of 500 m² or less; a secondary suite is permitted in the ALR only within the principal residence; and an additional detached residence may be up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less and up to 186 m² on properties over 40 ha. ALR status for any specific Sumas Prairie parcel: Not verified — check parcel by parcel.

Zoning frame: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 applies city-wide, including its agricultural zones. The City's AgRefresh parcel-size work records a minimum subdivision lot area of 8.0 ha in the Agricultural One Zone (A1) and 16.0 ha in the Agricultural Two Zone (A2) — so most prairie parcels cannot be split further in any form, strata or fee-simple. The zone of any specific parcel is a per-parcel check: Not verified for any individual parcel.

Suites and coach/garden suites: under Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014, a secondary suite must be less than 50% of the size of the principal unit, and garden suites and coach houses may occupy up to 15% of the lot area to a maximum of 100 m² — subject on ALR land to the ALC frame above (suite only within the principal residence).
City plan: the current Official Community Plan is Abbotsforward 2050, adopted December 2025 (see the currency note at the top) — the 2016 OCP is not current.

GST and taxes on a prairie purchase: 5% GST applies to new construction, not resales — prairie stock is resale farm/residential product. The First-Time Home Buyers' GST/HST Rebate (Bill C-4) rebates 100% of GST up to a $1 million price (maximum $50,000), phasing out to $1.5 million, for agreements signed on or after March 20, 2025 and before 2031; CRA's Excise and GST/HST News No. 122 states Bill C-4 received Royal Assent on March 13, 2026. The older GST New Housing Rebate (36%, maximum $6,300, $350,000–$450,000 phase-out) still exists.

blocks.text: Good to know about Sumas Prairie

items.t: The zero is structural, not a slow month. Sumas Prairie's attached row is empty because its land base is farm land under an ALR frame that bars stratification outright — a buyer waiting for a prairie condo project is waiting for a form the governing rules do not produce.
A buyer using the page's names and address will not find either school.

The flood-mitigation money is real, and the plan is still unfinished. Approximately $220 million in provincial funding since 2021 and $76.6 million for the Barrowtown Pump Station sound like a settled fix; the City-hosted release is explicit that the initiative's hydraulic model, risk assessment, ecological assessment and pump-station studies are at various stages of completion, and that December flooding again demonstrated the corridor's exposure. Price the prairie as flood land first, mitigation second.

The sub-area a buyer sees is wider than the prairie floor. Cards labelled "Sumas Prairie" include Majuba Hill and Old Yale Road upland acreage — a hillside house on the fringe carries a different flood and slope profile than a farm parcel on the floor, even though both wear the same sub-area label. Check the individual parcel, not the label.
The prairie's board row and its live feed describe different shelves.

The feed's own cards describe septic systems and wells property by property — there is no urban servicing assumption to fall back on, and each system's records have to be pulled for the specific property.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Sumas Prairie

items.t: OCP — CURRENT, with stale citations flagged: Abbotsforward 2050 is the CURRENT Official Community Plan, adopted December 2025.

Zoning / subdivision (Abbotsford): Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 applies city-wide, including its agricultural zones; the City's AgRefresh parcel-size work records minimum subdivision lot areas of 8.0 ha (A1) and 16.0 ha (A2). The zone of any specific parcel is a per-parcel check: Not verified for any individual parcel.

: The bylaw's s.140 provision allows 3 units on lots 280 m² or less and 4 units on lots greater than 280 m² in the stated conditions. How SSMUH applies on ALR prairie parcels is a per-parcel question and is not stated.

Suites and coach/garden suites (Abbotsford's rules ONLY): under Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014, a secondary suite must be less than 50% of the size of the principal unit (the cap is under 50%), s.140.3.8 permits one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings, and garden suites and coach houses may occupy up to 15% of the lot area to a maximum of 100 m² — the 15% / 100 m² coach/garden figure is Abbotsford's rule only, never exported to another municipality — subject on ALR land to the ALC frame below.

ALR block (full — this is dyked-prairie farm ground): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); land in the ALR may generally have no more than one residence per parcel unless the owner qualifies for an additional residence; caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is THREE tiers — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. ALR status for any specific Sumas Prairie parcel: Not verified — check parcel by parcel on the ALC maps.

Bare-land strata block (stated for completeness — no Sumas Prairie bare-land strata is verified): Form B (SPA s.59) within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page, with rules, budget and most recent depreciation report attached; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since Jul 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since Nov 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since Nov 24, 2022 (short-term may still be restricted); only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss.123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions) — a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw. Prairie farm and acreage purchases are fee-simple: NO strata, NO Form B, NO strata fees.
